title: Touch on-foot: fix the NaN-BigInt terrain error, get touch-onfoot.spec.ts fully green
description: Pick up TASK-93 where the third attempt stopped (handoff: `.ralph/handoff/TASK-93.md`, committed in 8eb9320 — read it first). Step 1 (implementation) is committed at 7cf56bf and unit-verified; leg 4 (RE-ENTER) steering is committed at 8eb9320 and VERIFIED CONVERGING (dist 11.39 → 6.54 → 2.98 m in 4 passes) after a nudge-sign flip. The spec `app/tests/e2e/touch-onfoot.spec.ts` is currently NOT green: once the character has walked to ~3 m of the ship (steering passes i≥4), the page throws ~16× `RangeError: The number NaN cannot be converted to a BigInt because it is not an integer` with stack `BigInt ← latticeValue (src/shared/galaxy/noise.ts:52) ← valueNoise (noise.ts:63) ← fbm01 (noise.ts:77) ← generateSurfaceChunk (src/shared/galaxy/surface.ts:259)`, and `collectErrors().assertClean()` (app/tests/e2e/helpers.ts) fails on ANY pageerror. The mechanism is traced: on foot, the terrain streamer is fed the CLIENT-PREDICTED character position — WorldManager (app/src/client/world/WorldManager.ts ~lines 799-825: on foot, `feed` = characterMesh.position → `terrainStreamer.update(feed.x, feed.z, speed)`) — and the mesh is driven every frame by the on-foot prediction loop (app/src/client/main.tsx ~1650-1691: `p.step(...)` → `world.setCharacterTransform(st.pos, ...)`). A NaN/Infinity predicted position → NaN chunkX/chunkZ → `Math.floor(NaN)` → `BigInt(NaN)` throws in noise.ts. (The server-authoritative position lives in `window.__CHAR__.pos`, the 10 Hz dev hook char-debug.ts — it is a SEPARATE channel from the predicted one.) THIS TASK: diagnose which position went non-finite, confirm it is not a pre-existing flake of other on-foot specs, and fix it SPEC-SIDE (steering geometry) so the character never reaches the bad path. No product code changes.

steps.details: First baseline: run the spec once as-is: `cd app && npx playwright test touch-onfoot.spec.ts --config playwright.e2e.config.ts --reporter=line` (single test, 180 s internal timeout, ~2-4 min per run — the e2eServer fixture boots its own dev server per spec file; never run alongside `npm run dev`). Record the exact failure (expected: steering loop exhausts its 60 passes or times out, then `assertClean()` lists the NaN-BigInt pageerrors). Then, in order: (a) TEMPORARY in-loop probe (re-add what iteration 8 removed): in the leg-4 loop, log per pass the `window.__CHAR__` pos (server-authoritative) with finiteness, AND the predicted mesh position if cheaply reachable — a one-line console.log of `st.pos` in the on-foot prediction loop (main.tsx ~1690, revert before commit) settles it: if the SERVER pos stays finite while the page throws the NaN chunk error, the culprit is the PREDICTED pos (st.pos / characterMesh.position). Check y specifically: a walk burst with a ~94°-off-axis facing (the measured state at pass i=4) from ~6.5 m out can carry the character PAST the ship and off the pad disc (PAD_RADIUS = 4, src/shared/physics/flight.ts; the pad disc blends into real terrain) into terrain where the ground blend can produce a non-finite sample. (b) Pre-existing flake check: `cd app && npx playwright test enter-ship.spec.ts walk.spec.ts --config playwright.e2e.config.ts` — the same keyboard walk-approach; if they throw the same BigInt pageerror, the trigger is generic (any on-foot walk near the pad edge), which confirms the spec-side geometry fix is the right scope. (c) Note: the streamer's TASK-84 island clip (`allowed()` in app/src/client/world/chunks.ts) filters out-of-island chunks, so a finite-but-far position is NOT the source — the coordinate must be non-finite (NaN or Infinity).

steps.description: Fix the leg-4 steering geometry, spec-side only
steps.details: Expected fix (handoff next-steps 2c): in leg 4 of app/tests/e2e/touch-onfoot.spec.ts, size the HIDDEN-ALIGNED WALK burst (the `Math.abs(angle) <= 0.79` branch, currently `((dist - 2.5) / 3) * 1000`) to land ~3.5 m from the ship instead of ~2.5 m — that keeps the character inside the 3-5 m '[E] Open cargo' sub-prompt zone (in cone, 3-5 m out) and lets the existing prompt branch do the final 1.8 m approach; it stops the character from crossing the ship/pad edge and cuts exposure to the yaw-release tail (a 100 ms yaw nudge on this software-GL page swings ~70-90° with the release event delayed 400-600 ms; `charSettled()` measures position only, not facing). If the diagnosis (step 1) shows a different trigger — e.g. overshoot in the 'Open cargo' branch, or leg 2's 2.5 s thrust walk leaving the character off the return line — size THAT burst the same way. Hard constraints: keep the nudge-sign convention `dir = angle > 0 ? -1 : 1` (measured, see notes), keep the 0.79 rad walk-band and 60-pass cap, and change ONLY the spec file. Do NOT touch the on-foot prediction loop, character physics, terrain streamer (chunks.ts), noise.ts/surface.ts, InteractableRegistry, or the server. If the diagnosis reveals a genuine product bug (NaN in the predictor or the terrain path), do NOT fix it here — work around it with the geometry and record the bug in the commit message so it can be split into its own task.

`cd app && npx playwright test touch-onfoot.spec.ts --config playwright.e2e.config.ts --reporter=line` FULLY GREEN: all 4 legs (1 layout: on-foot TouchControls visible + flight sticks/combat cluster absent; 2a MOVE thrust ≥ 4 m server-side + on the pad plane; 2b yaw burst turns the nose; 3 MINE: interrupted hold awards nothing + full hold awards 1/40u; 4 RE-ENTER: '[E] Enter ship' prompt holds, interactPress() re-enters, docked HUD stubs return, on-foot layout gone) AND zero console/page errors (assertClean). The spec itself writes `.ralph/screenshots/TASK-93-1.png` (it exists untracked from iteration 8's partial run — the green run rewrites it); verify it shows the on-foot touch layout with the interact prompt up. Remove ALL temporary probes: `git diff app/src app/tests/e2e/fixtures.ts` must be EMPTY and the spec diff must be clean code (no listeners/probes/logs). `cd app && npx tsc --noEmit` green. Commit ONLY the task files: spec + the rewritten screenshot — `wip(TASK-93): touch-onfoot e2e green — leg-4 NaN-BigInt fixed (steering geometry, spec-side)`. Exclude every pre-existing dirty file (see notes).

DEAD ENDS — do not retry: (a) nudging TOWARD the signed bearing (`dir = angle > 0 ? 1 : -1`, the intuitive choice) ping-pongs forever — measured on the live page: a yaw +1 burst ADDS ~+1.3-1.7 rad to the bearing angle (every transition fit within 0.15 rad); dist stuck at 11.69/11.99 m for all 60 passes. (b) burst-length does NOT control turn amount: a 100 ms yaw burst turns ~70-90° total on this software-GL page (the release event is queued 400-600 ms behind by the main thread), not ~17° — only nudge when |bearing| > 45° and walk when ≤ 45°. (c) server-side console probing is dead: the e2e fixture swallows server stdio (`bootServer` in app/tests/e2e/fixtures.ts); the client `__CHAR__` (server-authoritative, 10 Hz) is the steering signal. (d) `charPos` 15 s timeout with `__CHAR__.pos` null occurred once pre-sign-flip (character spinning in place at 11.99 m); did not reproduce after the flip — if it recurs, probe `__CHAR__` state (pos-null vs hook missing vs non-finite) in-loop.
Timing budget (45 min): one spec run ~2-4 min. Plan: baseline run + per-pass probe run ~10 min; enter-ship/walk flake check ~5 min; fix + 2-3 re-runs ~15 min; probe cleanup + tsc + commit ~5 min.

Commands: spec = `cd app && npx playwright test touch-onfoot.spec.ts --config playwright.e2e.config.ts --reporter=line`; flake check = `cd app && npx playwright test enter-ship.spec.ts walk.spec.ts --config playwright.e2e.config.ts`; typecheck = `cd app && npx tsc --noEmit`. Conventional commit: `wip(TASK-93): ...`

Leg-4 geometry reference (from the spec + iteration 8 measurements): ship docked at `target.pad` (from GET /api/dev/pad-target); docked-ship prompt zones: ≤ 3 m '[E] Enter ship', 3-5 m '[E] Open cargo' (in the 30° cone), > 5 m hidden; walk = 3 u/s; burst sized `((dist - landDist) / 3) * 1000` ms clamped 150-1500 ms; the release coast adds ~1 m. At the verified-converging pass i=4 the character was 2.98 m out but 94° off-axis — the next nudge's walk burst is where the run died with the NaN pageerrors.
